evals.name: audit-sweep-on-rename
evals.prompt: I renamed the skill /verify to /verify-changes. Find every stale reference.
evals.expected_output: Runs an audit sweep with the full pattern library (not a single token grep), triages hits into Certain / Chain-context / Ambiguous buckets, and reports them read-only. Old=`/verify`, new=`/verify-changes` parsed from the prose.
expectations: Output runs the full pattern-library sweep, not a single `/verify` token grep
Hits are triaged into the Certain / Chain-context / Ambiguous buckets
The audit is read-only (no edits applied in this audit invocation)

evals.name: never-trust-single-pattern-clean
evals.prompt: I ran `grep -r '/verify' .` and it came back with zero matches after my rename. That means the rename is clean, right?
evals.expected_output: Warns that a single-pattern grep returning clean is exactly the bug this skill exists to prevent — references survive in chain prose, comma-lists, numbered table rows, and frontmatter forms that token-only grep misses. It runs the full pattern library / audit rather than trusting the clean single-grep.
expectations: Output does NOT accept the zero-match single grep as proof the rename is clean
Output names syntactic forms (chain prose, comma-lists, numbered rows, frontmatter) that a token grep misses
Output recommends running the full pattern library / audit

evals.name: english-verb-forces-ambiguous-confirm
evals.prompt: Apply a rename of the skill `test` to `test e2e` across the repo.
evals.expected_output: Forces the bare `test` token into the Ambiguous bucket (English-verb blocklist) regardless of regex position and confirms each match with surrounding context rather than auto-applying — bare 'test' collides with ordinary English usage. It applies the most-specific match first to avoid double-editing the substring expansion.
expectations: The bare `test` token is routed to the Ambiguous bucket and confirmed per-match, not auto-applied
Output cites the English-verb collision as the reason for mandatory confirmation
Output does not blindly replace every `test` occurrence in prose

evals.name: re-sweep-until-zero-new-form-learned
evals.prompt: You applied the /verify to /verify-changes rename. The re-sweep still finds one match in a frontmatter glob form the pattern library didn't have. What now?
evals.expected_output: Does not declare done: re-sweep must reach an actionable count of 0. The new syntactic form is a pattern-library gap — it adds the form to the pattern registry, re-iterates the sweep, and does NOT silently apply or ignore the straggler.
expectations: Output does NOT declare the rename complete while the re-sweep count is non-zero
Output treats the new form as a pattern-library gap to add, then re-sweeps
Output does not silently apply or drop the remaining match

evals.name: refuse-framework-migration
evals.prompt: Use rename-references to migrate our test project from xUnit v2 to xUnit v3 — update all the APIs.
evals.expected_output: Declines: framework version migrations are a behavioral upgrade, not a text rename, and are out of scope. It points to dedicated migration tooling and clarifies the skill handles documentation / config / identifier-string renames, not AST-level or API migrations.
expectations: Output declines the framework migration as out of scope
Output distinguishes a behavioral/API migration from a text-string rename
Output points to dedicated migration tooling instead of running its sweep

evals.name: plan-doc-auto-excluded
evals.prompt: Apply the /verify to /verify-changes rename. Note the active plan doc PLAN.md documents this very rename and mentions both names on purpose.
evals.expected_output: Auto-excludes the rename-documenting plan doc from the sweep — both old and new names appear there by design, and editing it would break the migration narrative. Apply mode rejects `--include-plan-docs`; the plan doc is left untouched.
expectations: The active rename-documenting plan doc is auto-excluded and left unedited
Output explains both names appear in the plan doc by design (self-reference)
Output does not rewrite the plan doc's occurrences of the old name

evals.name: container-rename-catches-command-argument-and-title
evals.prompt: I renamed the plugin `re-anchor` to `discipline`. The directory moved and every qualified `/re-anchor:<skill>` invocation is already updated. Audit for anything still stale.
evals.expected_output: The sweep runs the container-position forms (13-15) in addition to Forms 1-12, so it reports the plugin name in command-argument position (`/plugin install re-anchor@acme-tools`, `/plugin configure re-anchor`), a document title that is the bare token (`# re-anchor`), and possessive container prose ("re-anchor's effective configuration") as Certain. It does NOT report the English-verb uses ("each skill re-anchors ONE discipline") as Certain, and it flags command-argument hits as functional breaks rather than cosmetic ones.
expectations: Forms 13-15 are run, not only the slash-token and path forms that a directory move already satisfies
`/plugin install <old>@marketplace` and `/plugin configure <old>` are reported as Certain and identified as functional breaks
A heading whose entire content is the bare token is reported as Certain
Verb-sense uses of the token are not swept into the Certain bucket

evals.name: verb-collision-not-fixed-by-blocklist-extension
evals.prompt: The token I'm renaming is also used as a verb hundreds of times in this repo. Should I add it to the English-verb blocklist so the sweep stops proposing bad rewrites?
evals.expected_output: Explains that blocklist extension is the wrong remedy for a token that is a verb in the consuming codebase: leaving it off rates every bare-token hit Certain, and adding it forces every hit into the ambiguous bucket where the per-match confirmation rule turns a handful of real defects into hundreds of prompts. Routes to the position-anchored forms 13-15 instead, which stay Certain regardless of blocklist membership because their surrounding syntax admits only the container sense.
expectations: Identifies that BOTH blocklist branches fail for a codebase-specific verb, not just the omit branch
Recommends position-anchored forms rather than extending the blocklist
Does not propose per-match confirmation over the full bare-token hit set as the answer

evals.name: container-position-match-supersedes-the-bare-token-it-covers
evals.prompt: Audit the rename of `re-anchor` to `discipline`. The token is also used as an English verb throughout the plugin, so I expect a lot of noise.
evals.expected_output: The sweep runs Form 2 and the container-position forms, then deduplicates by OCCURRENCE SPAN (file, line, start, end) before triage: a container-position match is attributed to its own form and enters that form's bucket after its scope rules apply, and the Form 2 match COVERED BY that span is dropped rather than raised as a second finding. A bare occurrence elsewhere on the same line is a different reference and survives. Occurrences Form 2 matched alone are ordinary verb uses and, under container-rename mode, are excluded from Certain and reported as an aggregate rather than as prompts. The report states how many Form-2 hits were superseded.
expectations: Deduplication keys on the occurrence span, never on line identity, and runs after the sweep and BEFORE triage
The bare-token match covered by a container-position span is dropped; an independent occurrence on the same line survives
A container-position match enters its own form's bucket after scope rules, which may be Ambiguous rather than Certain
The report includes the count of Form-2 hits superseded by container-position matches
Ordinary verb uses are not surfaced as rename candidates or as mandatory confirmation prompts

evals.name: container-mode-excludes-bare-token-residue-from-certain
evals.prompt: Audit the rename of the `re-anchor` plugin to `discipline`. The token is used as an English verb about 130 times across the plugin and it is not in the blocklist.
evals.expected_output: Declares container-rename mode at Phase 0. Position-anchored forms produce the Certain bucket; the bare-token residue -- every Form 2 line NOT matched by a position-anchored form -- is excluded from Certain entirely regardless of blocklist membership, and reported as a single aggregate count rather than as per-match confirmation prompts. It does not propose rewriting the verb uses, and it does not ask the user to confirm them one by one.
expectations: Container-rename mode is declared and drives the bucketing
Bare-token residue is excluded from Certain WITHOUT relying on the blocklist
Residue is reported as an aggregate count, not as per-match prompts
Deduplication of overlapping lines is not presented as sufficient on its own
The eligibility rule is applied as an allowlist over forms, so Forms 8 and 12 lose their Certain default too rather than only Form 2 being filtered

evals.name: title-form-scoped-to-container-owned-documents
evals.prompt: Rename the `testing` plugin to `test-suite`. Audit for stale references.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes that `testing` is an ordinary English word, so Form 14 TITLE matches are demoted to Ambiguous rather than Certain. A heading like `### Testing` in the repository root README (a marketplace category heading, not the container's own document) is NOT auto-applied; only headings in plausibly container-owned files -- the plugin's own README/SKILL/manifest or paths under its directory -- are eligible for Certain, and even those are demoted when the token is a common word. The scope rule and the common-word demotion govern the title alternatives only: the plugin's own manifest `"name": "testing"` declaration is still Certain, because a manifest name key is the registration rather than evidence of one and cannot be verb usage.
expectations: A title match outside container-owned files is not rated Certain
An ordinary-word container name demotes title matches regardless of path
Precedence does not discard the safer classification for an out-of-scope title match
The manifest name declaration is exempt from both demotions and stays Certain

evals.name: apply-mode-terminates-under-container-rename-mode
evals.prompt: Apply the rename of the `re-anchor` plugin to `discipline`. About 130 lines use the token as an ordinary English verb.
evals.expected_output: Phase 6's completion check uses the ACTIONABLE count -- the survey result after precedence and container-rename mode -- not the raw match count. The bare-token residue is deliberately left unrenamed, so it still matches the token forever; counting it raw would mean Outcome A is never reached and Outcome B loops indefinitely. Apply mode reaches Outcome A once no actionable matches remain, and reports the residue in the Phase 7 summary as the same aggregate the audit reports.
expectations: Completion is evaluated on the actionable count, not the raw match count
The re-sweep does not loop on residue the mode rule deliberately excluded
Residue is surfaced in the hand-off summary rather than silently dropped

evals.name: qualified-id-form-does-not-rewrite-email-addresses
evals.prompt: Rename the `info` plugin to `plugin-info`. The docs contain the contact address info@acmetools.com.
evals.expected_output: Form 13's qualified-id alternative matches the marketplace-qualified id (info@acme-tools) but NOT the email address (info@acmetools.com), because a marketplace slug is kebab-case with no dots while an email domain carries a TLD dot. The contact address is not proposed for rewriting and is not auto-applied.
expectations: The marketplace-qualified id is still matched
The email address is not matched and is never auto-rewritten
The distinction is made structurally by the pattern, not by asking the user to catch it

evals.name: span-dedup-preserves-a-second-reference-on-the-same-line
evals.prompt: Audit the rename of the `re-anchor` plugin to `discipline`. One line reads: Use re-anchor via /plugin install re-anchor@acme-tools
evals.expected_output: Both occurrences on that line are reported. Deduplication keys on the occurrence SPAN (file, line, start, end), not the whole line, so the command-argument match suppresses only the bare-token match COVERED BY its own span -- the other bare occurrence earlier in the line is a separate reference and survives. Collapsing by line would drop it, and since Phase 5 replaces one span at a time, the surviving reference would then be reclassified as residue and the re-sweep would declare completion with a live stale reference in the file.
expectations: Both references on the line are reported, not one
Suppression is by span coverage, never by line identity
The failure mode named is a false completion, not merely a missed report

evals.name: qualified-id-form-avoids-lookaround
evals.prompt: Run the rename sweep for a plugin named `info` using the Grep tool's default engine.
evals.expected_output: Form 13's qualified-id alternative runs on the default engine without requiring PCRE2. Its trailing boundary CONSUMES a terminator -- ([^\w.@-]|$) -- rather than using a negative lookahead, because ripgrep's default engine rejects look-around (it needs -P/--pcre2) and patterns.md's own cross-platform note already bans lookbehinds for the same reason. The consumed trailing character is not part of the reference and is left in place when replacing.
expectations: No look-around is used, so the form works on the default engine the skill instructs
The trailing terminator is consumed rather than asserted
A consumed delimiter is not rewritten as part of the reference

evals.name: container-position-demotion-survives-in-the-bucket-criteria
evals.prompt: Rename the `testing` plugin to `test-suite`. The repo root README has a `### Testing` category heading. Show me the triage buckets.
evals.expected_output: The `### Testing` heading is reported as Ambiguous, not Certain. triage.md's Ambiguous criteria list container-position Forms 14 and 15 as Ambiguous whenever the matching form's own scope rules demote it -- Form 13 is deliberately absent, its demoted alternative landing in Chain-context instead -- and audit.md's Certain definition carries the same qualifier -- so the demotion holds no matter which file the reader consults. Span-precedence attributes the occurrence to Form 14 and drops the bare-token duplicate, but does not override the demotion.
expectations: The out-of-scope title match lands Ambiguous in the reported buckets
The demotion is consistent whether read from triage.md or audit.md
Precedence attributes the occurrence without promoting it

evals.name: mode-is-resolved-by-evidence-not-defaulted
evals.prompt: /rename-references re-anchor to discipline
evals.expected_output: Phase 1 resolves the rename MODE before surveying, using the Phase 0b ladder rather than defaulting: it finds plugins/re-anchor/ (or plugins/discipline/ post-move, read from git) carrying a plugin manifest, and /re-anchor:<skill> namespaced invocations in the tree. It collects all three evidence rules rather than stopping at the first, finds them in agreement, and concludes container. The resolved mode and every rule that fired appear in the report. If no rule fires -- or if the rules disagree -- it asks the user rather than guessing, and it never infers mode from the token's shape (hyphenation or word-likeness).
expectations: Mode is resolved in Phase 1, before the survey and bucketing
Resolution cites concrete evidence -- directory/manifest/invocation shape -- not token appearance
An unresolvable case asks rather than silently defaulting either way
The report states the resolved mode and the rule that produced it

evals.name: coequal-form-alternatives-collapse-to-one-match
evals.prompt: Apply the rename of the `re-anchor` plugin to `discipline`. A line reads: /plugin install re-anchor@acme-tools
evals.expected_output: That occurrence is reported and edited ONCE. Both of Form 13's alternatives match it -- the management-verb alternative and the qualified-id alternative -- so span coverage collapses them to a single match (widest span preferred, earlier-numbered form on a tie) before triage. Left uncollapsed the count would double and Phase 5 would schedule two targeted Edits, the second failing because the first already rewrote the token.
expectations: One finding and one Edit for the single occurrence, not two
Collapsing applies within a form, not only between a stronger and a weaker form
The named failure is a failed second Edit plus an inflated count, not merely a cosmetic duplicate

evals.name: hyphenated-superstring-is-not-a-container-match
evals.prompt: Rename the `context` plugin to `session-context`. The repo also has a `context-guard` plugin referenced as /plugin configure context-guard and context-guard@acme-tools.
evals.expected_output: The `context-guard` references are NOT matched. Container IDs are kebab-case, so a plain word boundary would let `context` match inside the hyphenated superstring `context-guard` and auto-rewrite an unrelated plugin's identifier on a Certain-rated form. Forms 13 and 15 exclude an adjacent hyphen on both sides, so `/plugin configure context` and `context@acme-tools` match while `/plugin configure context-guard` and `context-guard@acme-tools` do not.
expectations: A hyphenated superstring containing the token is never matched as the container
The exact-name references are still matched
The failure prevented is auto-rewriting a DIFFERENT plugin's identifier, not a cosmetic over-match

evals.name: survey-emits-one-record-per-occurrence-not-per-line
evals.prompt: Audit the rename of `re-anchor` to `discipline`. A line reads: Use re-anchor via /plugin install re-anchor@acme-tools
evals.expected_output: Phase 2 emits TWO records for that line, one per occurrence, each carrying {file, line, start, end, pattern_form, snippet}. Grep's content mode returns matching LINES and --column reports only the first match on a line, so the survey re-scans each returned match locally for every occurrence before deduplication. Without per-occurrence offsets the span rule has nothing to compare and silently degrades to line-keyed dedup, restoring the false completion eval 14 prevents. The rescan unit is the returned MATCH, not always a line: for the two multiline forms (Form 7 and Form 14's Setext alternative) the block is kept intact and the pattern re-run against the whole block, because feeding those patterns one line at a time reproduces nothing and would drop the record entirely.
expectations: One record per occurrence, not per line
Records carry start/end offsets before deduplication runs
The stated failure is a silent degradation to line-keyed dedup, not a missing field

evals.name: marketplace-subcommand-is-matched
evals.prompt: Rename the marketplace `acme-tools` to `acme-plugins`. The README says /plugin marketplace add acme-tools and /plugin marketplace update acme-tools.
evals.expected_output: Both marketplace commands are matched by Form 13 as command-argument references. A marketplace name sits after `/plugin marketplace add|update` rather than directly after `/plugin`, so without the optional marketplace subcommand group they match no position-anchored form, container mode suppresses their Form 2 hits as residue, and the sweep reports zero actionable stragglers while executable install instructions stay stale.
expectations: /plugin marketplace add|update <old> is matched
A hyphenated superstring such as acme-tools-extra is not matched
The failure prevented is a false zero-straggler report on executable instructions

evals.name: bare-qualified-id-is-chain-context-not-certain
evals.prompt: Rename the `t` plugin to `toolkit`. The repo contains git config user.email t@t in test fixtures.
evals.expected_output: The bare qualified-id alternative is rated Chain-context, not Certain, so `t@t` is not auto-applied. Excluding dots is necessary but not sufficient -- a dotless address is still a valid address, and this tree contains both `auth_email: "a@b"` and `user.email t@t`. The management-verb alternative stays Certain because its verb anchors it. The unanchored alternative is promoted to Certain only by a per-occurrence structural signal -- the occurrence IS a key in an enabledPlugins/pluginConfigs map -- never by a management verb elsewhere on the line, which may govern an entirely different plugin.
expectations: The unanchored qualified-id form does not auto-apply
The management-verb alternative keeps its Certain rating
Dot-exclusion is described as insufficient rather than sufficient
The Chain-context rating survives span-precedence and container-rename mode rather than being flattened back to Certain
A failed promotion check leaves the alternative at Chain-context rather than dropping it to Ambiguous

evals.name: mode-override-flags-are-parseable
evals.prompt: /rename-references audit context to session-context --identifier
evals.expected_output: The flag parses and forces identifier-rename mode, skipping the Phase 0b evidence ladder. Both --container and --identifier are registered in SKILL.md's argument-hint and flag table and in audit-modes.md's override table, so the documented correction mechanism is honored rather than rejected as an unknown flag. Passing both is an error, not a precedence question.
expectations: --identifier and --container are accepted, not rejected as unknown flags
They are honored in audit, preview, and apply
Passing both is an explicit error

evals.name: coequal-collapse-keys-on-the-captured-token-span
evals.prompt: Apply the rename of `re-anchor` to `discipline`. A line reads: /plugin install re-anchor@acme-tools
evals.expected_output: One finding, one Edit. Deduplication keys on the CAPTURED <old> span, not the whole match span: Form 13's management-verb alternative spans `/plugin install <old>@` while its qualified-id alternative spans `<old>@acme-tools`, which overlap without either containing the other -- so a whole-span coverage test would keep both and schedule two Edits on one token, the second failing because the first already rewrote it.
expectations: Coverage is tested on the captured token span, not the full match span
Two overlapping non-containing matches on one token collapse to one
The named failure is a failed second Edit, not a duplicate report line

evals.name: setext-title-is-a-container-title-match
evals.prompt: Rename the `re-anchor` plugin to `discipline`. Its README titles itself with `re-anchor` underlined by `=====` rather than an ATX heading.
evals.expected_output: Form 14 matches the Setext title shape (the token alone on a line followed by a line of = or -), so the container's own landing-page title is reported. Without it the title's only hit is Form 2, which container mode excludes as residue, and the rename could report completion with the primary title stale. Requires multiline matching, like Form 7.
expectations: The Setext title shape is recognized as a title match
Multiline matching is used
The failure prevented is a completion report with a stale landing-page title

evals.name: sentence-initial-appositive-is-matched
evals.prompt: Rename the `guard` plugin to `guardrails`. The docs say: The guard plugin ships two hooks.
evals.expected_output: Form 15's appositive alternative matches the sentence-initial `The`, not only a lowercase `the`. Otherwise the token's only hit is Form 2, which container mode suppresses as residue, and apply mode finishes with the stale container reference. Only the article is case-flexible; the token itself stays case-sensitive, and `The context-guard plugin` is still rejected as a hyphenated superstring.
expectations: Sentence-initial `The` is matched as well as lowercase `the`
The token remains case-sensitive
A hyphenated superstring is still not matched

evals.name: json-manifest-name-declaration-is-a-container-position-match
evals.prompt: Rename the `docs-hygiene` plugin to `doc-care`. Its manifest is JSON: .claude-plugin/marketplace.json carries `"name": "docs-hygiene"` indented inside an entry, and plugins/docs-hygiene/.claude-plugin/plugin.json carries the same at line 3. Audit for stale references.
evals.expected_output: Form 14's JSON declaration alternative matches both, so the container's registered name is reported as Certain. The YAML alternative is anchored at column zero with an unquoted key and reaches neither; without the JSON alternative no container-position form reaches them, container mode reduces both to excluded Form-2 residue, and the sweep can report zero actionable stragglers while the plugin stays registered under its old name. The scope rule does not demote the marketplace entry for living at the repository root rather than under the container's directory -- a catalog entry is the container's registration, and the quoted `name` key is the proof, so it is exempt from the container-owned-path test.
expectations: The indented, quoted JSON name declaration is matched
The repository-root catalog entry is rated Certain rather than demoted for being outside the container's directory
The failure prevented is a completion report with the registered container name stale

evals.name: terminal-container-directory-path-stays-actionable
evals.prompt: Rename the `docs-hygiene` plugin to `doc-care`. The catalog says `"source": "./plugins/docs-hygiene"` and the root README links `[docs-hygiene](plugins/docs-hygiene)`. Audit for stale references.
evals.expected_output: Form 3's container-root alternative matches both. The earlier path alternatives all require something after the token -- a .md extension, a trailing slash, a known subdirectory -- so a path that ENDS in the container name reaches none of them; container mode then excludes the only remaining hit as bare-token residue and apply mode can finish while the marketplace points at a directory that no longer exists and installation is broken. The alternative excludes an adjacent hyphen at both ends, so `plugins/docs-hygiene-extra` and `x-plugins/docs-hygiene` do not match, and its parent segment is a bounded container-root vocabulary rather than any path segment, because an unconstrained parent would match ordinary prose like `input/output` on a Certain-rated form.
expectations: A path terminating in the container name is matched
Hyphenated superstrings on either side are not matched
The parent segment is bounded to a container-root vocabulary rather than any segment
The failure prevented is apply mode completing with the catalog pointing at a vanished directory

evals.name: setext-alternative-is-multiline-enabled-in-the-survey
evals.prompt: During the Phase 2 survey I enabled `multiline: true` only for Form 7, the way the survey step lists it. Is Form 14 going to work?
evals.expected_output: No. Form 14's Setext alternative contains a literal \n, and ripgrep's single-line default rejects that outright -- it errors with `the literal "\n" is not allowed in a regex` rather than simply matching nothing. The survey step lists Form 14's Setext alternative alongside Form 7 as requiring multiline for exactly this reason; run without it the pattern is not executable at all, the survey silently loses the form, and a container's landing-page title survives as Form-2 residue that container mode excludes from Certain.
expectations: Multiline is identified as required for Form 14's Setext alternative, not only Form 7
The failure mode is a regex error rather than a silent under-match
The consequence named is a stale landing-page title reported as completion

evals.name: toml-manifest-name-declaration-is-matched
evals.prompt: Rename the Python package `docs-hygiene` to `doc-care`. Its pyproject.toml declares `name = "docs-hygiene"` under [project]. Audit for stale references.
evals.expected_output: Form 14's TOML declaration alternative matches it. TOML delimits with `=` rather than `:`, so both the YAML and the JSON alternatives miss it -- and because the mode ladder names pyproject.toml as manifest evidence for selecting CONTAINER mode, missing it routes the package into the mode that suppresses bare-token residue while leaving the one declaration that mode makes load-bearing unmatched: apply mode reports zero actionable stragglers with the package metadata still carrying the old name. The alternative accepts an optionally-quoted key and a basic or literal string value, and rejects `name = "docs-hygiene-extra"` and `description = "docs-hygiene"`. Because pyproject.toml is a manifest, the declaration is exempt from the title scope rule and the common-word demotion; the same `name="..."` shape in a shell script is NOT, since the exemption is conditioned on the file being a manifest or catalog.
expectations: The `=`-delimited TOML declaration is matched, not only the `:`-delimited YAML and JSON shapes
The contradiction named is that the mode ladder already treats pyproject.toml as container evidence
The manifest/catalog condition on the exemption is preserved, so shell assignment syntax is not swept in as Certain

evals.name: qualified-id-promotion-binds-to-the-occurrence-not-the-line
evals.prompt: Rename the `t` plugin to `toolkit`. A doc line reads: /plugin install foo@acme; email t@t
evals.expected_output: `t@t` stays Chain-context and is not auto-applied. The line does carry a management verb, but it governs `foo@acme`, a different plugin -- so a line-level promotion test would rate the unrelated address Certain and apply mode would rewrite it, which is the exact failure the demotion exists to prevent. A verb that actually governs an occurrence is already matched by the management-verb alternative and already Certain, so a line-level check adds no recall and only launders the demotion. The only promotion signal is structural and per-occurrence: the occurrence IS a key in an enabledPlugins/pluginConfigs map.
expectations: The unrelated management verb on the same line does not promote the address
`/plugin install foo@acme` is still reported as a Certain reference in its own right when `foo` is the renamed token
The promotion signal named is per-occurrence and structural, not line-level

evals.name: conflicting-mode-evidence-asks-instead-of-taking-first-match
evals.prompt: Rename the `/test` action to `/verify`. Somewhere in this monorepo an unrelated package manifest declares name = "test". Which mode does the sweep pick?
evals.expected_output: Neither, unasked. Manifest evidence (rule 3) says container and invocation-shape evidence (rule 4) says identifier, and only the explicit --container/--identifier override short-circuits the ladder -- rules 2 through 4 are evidence to be collected in full and compared, not a precedence order. Taking the earliest would select container mode, whose residue rule suppresses exactly the bare `/test` references that are actionable here, and the rename would falsely complete. On disagreement the sweep falls through to the ask, showing each rule's verdict and the file that produced it. A shared string is not evidence the manifest and the invocation name the same entity; correlation is established from the tree (a manifest whose directory also contains the /<old> definition) or not assumed at all.
expectations: Conflicting evidence routes to the user rather than resolving by ladder order
The named risk is container mode suppressing actionable identifier references
A shared name is not treated as evidence that the two rules describe the same entity

evals.name: manifest-id-declaration-is-matched-like-name
evals.prompt: Rename the `docs-hygiene` container to `doc-care`. Its manifest identifies it with an `id` field rather than `name`. Audit for stale references.
evals.expected_output: All three of Form 14's declaration alternatives accept `id` alongside `name` and `title`, so the declaration is matched and reported as Certain. The mode ladder already selects CONTAINER mode on `<old>` appearing as the name/id field of a manifest, so recognizing only `name` and `title` routed such a manifest into the mode that suppresses bare-token residue while leaving its `id` occurrence as excluded residue -- apply mode could then report zero actionable stragglers with the manifest still registering the old ID. The manifest/catalog condition on the exemption is what keeps the widened key set safe: `id="$1"` is ordinary shell assignment syntax and appears dozens of times in this repository, so outside a manifest an `id` match is treated as a title match and takes the scope rule and the common-word demotion rather than becoming a Certain rename candidate.
expectations: An `id` declaration is matched, not only `name` and `title`
The contradiction named is that the mode ladder already treats an `id` field as container evidence
Shell `id=` assignments outside a manifest are not rated Certain

evals.name: catalog-keyed-by-container-id-is-matched
evals.prompt: Rename the `docs-hygiene` plugin to `doc-care`. The registry is keyed by container id rather than carrying a name field: plugins: { "docs-hygiene": { ... } }. Audit for stale references.
evals.expected_output: Form 14's key-position alternative matches the catalog key. The mode ladder already names both catalog shapes -- the name/id field of a manifest OR a key in a marketplace/registry catalog -- so recognizing only the field shape selected container mode while the registry's own key stayed unmatched Form-2 residue and apply mode could report zero actionable stragglers with the registry still using the old ID. The alternative requires the value to OPEN an object or array, which is what distinguishes a catalog entry from an ordinary scalar setting. Its manifest/catalog condition is mandatory rather than merely helpful: `"<key>": {` is the commonest line shape in JSON -- this repository carries 569 of them -- so outside a file established as a manifest or registry catalog the match is Ambiguous unconditionally.
expectations: A catalog key naming the container is matched, not only a name/id field
The value must open an object or array, distinguishing a catalog entry from a scalar setting
The alternative is Ambiguous outside a manifest or catalog file, with no common-word exception needed

evals.name: container-mode-allowlist-demotes-glob-and-dot-forms
evals.prompt: Rename the `context` plugin to `context-tools`. The repo has a config key `context.timeout` and a frontmatter glob `{a,context,b}` enumerating skills. Audit in container mode.
evals.expected_output: Neither is rated Certain. Container mode's eligibility rule is an ALLOWLIST over forms -- Forms 1, 3 and 13-15 are the whole Certain-eligible set -- not a filter on Form 2 alone. Applied only to the bare-token residue it would leave Form 12 (dot-form) and Form 8 (glob set) on the auto-apply path, and both are Certain by default, so apply mode would rewrite the unrelated dotted key and the glob entry. Those forms anchor on syntax proving the token is an IDENTIFIER, which is exactly what a container rename is not asking about, so they demote to Ambiguous. They are demoted and reported per match rather than aggregated like the bare-token residue, because they are few and a container name genuinely can appear in a glob set.
expectations: Forms 8 and 12 lose their Certain default under container mode
The rule is described as an allowlist over forms rather than a Form 2 filter
The demoted matches are reported per match, not folded into the bare-token aggregate

evals.name: multiline-matches-are-rescanned-as-blocks
evals.prompt: In Phase 2 I rescan every returned line with the form's own pattern to emit per-occurrence records. Does that work for Form 7 and Form 14's Setext alternative?
evals.expected_output: No, and the failure is silent. Those two patterns match only against a multi-line block, so re-running them against one line at a time reproduces nothing, no per-occurrence record is emitted, and the reference disappears between the survey and triage -- on exactly the two forms that exist because their references were being missed. The survey keeps the matched block intact, runs the pattern against the whole block, locates the captured <old> span within it, and converts that block offset to (line, start, end) using the block's first-line number. Line-by-line rescanning stays correct for every single-line form; the branch is whether the form requires multiline matching, which is the same two forms.
expectations: The multiline forms are rescanned as blocks rather than line by line
The named failure is a dropped record, silently, rather than a partial match
The block offset is converted back to a line-relative span so dedup still works
